arms.description: Control, no faults: the parallel-sweep-2 baseline at 720 s (lead, eight workers with four modules each, a synthesiser that reads the sheet files); cost, time and delivery only

The hand-off layer as the only path: the synthesiser cannot read out/<module>/, reads the eight published documents, decides accept or reject on each before use, with four harness-seeded faults (one class each) injected at first publish; rejections are relayed synthesiser to lead to worker

writer_authority: each module sheet is written only by the worker that owns the module and the synthesis only by the synthesiser; the corpus is read-only in both arms; in the treatment arm each worker also publishes its four sheets as one document (module-sheets-w<k>), the files being what is scored and the documents being what the synthesiser reads; only the harness's injector changes a published document

fault_injection.scope: treatment arm of this scenario only; each document is changed once, at its first successful publish; the change is recorded as a fault event in the store's event log

staged_plan.status: APPROVED 2026-10-04 by the lead, under the owner's standing instruction: stage 1 only is started; stage 2 starts only if the stage 1 mechanism gate passed
staged_plan.basis: docs/mastermind/pilot/2026-10-04-parallel-sweep-3-design.md; all USD in harness dollars (1.5x the Sonnet 5.5 list rates, to be reconciled by the owner)

stages.run: node smoke/prepare.mjs inputs --scenario parallel-sweep-3 --base <base>; PILOT_ALLOCATION_USD=25 PILOT_ONLY=parallel-sweep-3:treatment:1:0 pilot/run-all.sh <base> <cli.js>
stages.measures: whether the synthesiser reads and decides on the published documents at all (the mechanism gate), and the first read of faults caught and missed

trials.optional: a no-fault control for cost, time and delivery; the sweep-2 baseline rerun already is one at 600 s; dropping it saves about $16

stages.run: PILOT_ALLOCATION_USD=80 PILOT_ONLY=parallel-sweep-3:treatment:2:0,parallel-sweep-3:baseline:1:0 pilot/run-all.sh <base> <cli.js> (the same <base>; pilot/stage-gate.mjs refuses it unless the stage 1 gate passed)
stages.gate: only if, in the stage 1 treatment trial, the synthesiser made at least one successful pilot__doc_read call
stages.measures: a second fault placement (a different seed), the decision measures at n=2, and the cost and time of the control

stages.note: not planned; a further owner approval; nothing in stage 3 starts without it

estimate_cheapest_pilot_usd.what: stage 1 plus the second treatment trial only (no baseline control)

staged_plan.estimate_basis: harness dollars from the parallel-sweep-2 rerun (treatment 14.13 with the synthesiser at 0.40 and the lead at 0.43; baseline 18.17); the synthesiser is estimated at 1.2 / 2.4 / 3.0 (its cap) for about 50 to 70 turns on a growing context plus spot checks, the lead at 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.4 for the relays, and four republishes at about 0.25 each

stop_rule.mechanism_gate: After the first treatment trial: if the synthesiser made 0 successful pilot__doc_read calls, the mechanism failed: stop and report; no further trial starts (stage-gate.mjs refuses stage 2 and stage 3). A trial in which the synthesiser never started counts as 0 reads.
stop_rule.not_a_gate: Reads with 0 decides, or 0 faults caught, do not stop the pilot; they are the result and are reported to the lead.
stop_rule.per_trial_stop: the org-wide $34 spend stop (spend-stop.mjs), the 720 s deadline, or the lead's org_complete, whichever comes first
stop_rule.soft_caps: stage 1 25 USD, the pilot 80 USD (run-all.sh stops without starting another trial once the spend so far passes PILOT_ALLOCATION_USD); the owner's plan line is about 150 USD

thresholds.spend_flag_basis: the high estimate of a treatment trial; a trial above it is reported before another starts

predictions: The synthesiser reads all eight documents and decides on all eight (the gate asks only for one read). Not tested before.
It catches the cheap classes (reversed files lists, a copied sheet) at a higher rate than the wrong values, which need a hand trace of a call chain.
At least one of two treatment trials delivers 31 or more of the 33 units, with the synthesis file written between 400 and 650 s.
stop_rule.unit: units accepted by the 720 s deadline, of 33; the decision measures are in units.json under handoff
stop_rule.exploratory: harness-only prototype, exploratory, n=2 at most per arm, no intervals; it cannot pass or fail the coordination gate or qualify defaults

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: A new scenario, parallel-sweep-3, next to parallel-sweep-2: the same 32-module, 8-worker, 33-unit workload (same corpus generator and seed, truth, scorer, roster, per-worker caps, no-node sandbox and home write-deny) reshaped so that the synthesiser must read and decide on the published module documents, built unpaid and test-first. Fixture record: tests/eval/org/fixtures/parallel-sweep-3/fixture.json.
declared_changes.why: The parallel-sweep-2 stage 2 rerun ran only the write side of the hand-off layer (eight doc_publish, zero doc_read, doc_decide or doc_list): the synthesiser aggregated the workers' sheet files with jq, so the layer itself, the read and the decision, was never measured.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none rewritten: parallel-sweep and parallel-sweep-2, their pinned hashes, manifests and results stay as they are

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: Treatment arm: the synthesiser cannot read out/m1 .. out/m32 (policy.sandbox.denyRead, the bubblewrap layer that already hides the truth) and receives the module sheets only through pilot__doc_read; it must call pilot__doc_decide (accept, or reject with a reason) on each document before using it, and keeps read access to corpus/ so it can check a claim against the code. The trial's pilot-state/ and trial.json and the tests/eval/org tree are hidden from every role so no role can read the fault plan or the injector. The task text tells it the documents may contain errors and what a decision means, not which documents are corrupted.
declared_changes.why: Makes the hand-off channel the only path, so a run cannot bypass it by aggregating files.
declared_changes.earlier_result: the sweep-2 treatment rerun (33 of 33 in 297 s, no read or decide calls) stays on record

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: The pilot harness gains a deterministic, seeded fault hook (pilot/fault-injection.ts, applied by HandoffStore.publish through a PublishInjector, set only by a pilot manifest's fault_injection and only in that scenario's treatment arm): 4 of the 8 worker documents are changed at their first successful publish, one class each (a wrong q05 value, a wrong q07 value, reversed files lists, a sheet replaced by a copy of another module's), each only once; the producer's own files in out/ stay correct, so a republished document is correct. Every change is recorded in the store's event log as a `fault` event, from which the report counts faults caught, missed and false rejects. Seed: seed_base 20261003 plus the trial number.
declared_changes.why: Makes the decisions matter and their quality measurable. The faults are harness-injected, so this measures the decision path, not natural errors.
declared_changes.earlier_result: no other scenario or arm sets fault_injection; every existing pilot trial is unchanged

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: The wall deadline of this scenario is 720 s (twelve minutes), not 600 s, in both arms; the per-run planning allocation and org stop are $34 (harness dollars) because the synthesiser and lead caps rise (synthesiser $3.0, lead $1.4 at the production profile).
declared_changes.why: The sweep-2 treatment rerun ended at 297 s with the last document at about 275 s; reads, spot checks, a relayed rejection, a republish and a second decision add an estimated 150 to 300 s, and at 600 s a late republish would be cut by the deadline so that the trial measured the clock, not the decisions.
declared_changes.earlier_result: parallel-sweep-2 keeps its 600 s design; its times are comparable only indicatively

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: The baseline arm is the sweep-2 baseline at 720 s with no fault injection: the synthesiser reads the workers' sheet files. It is a control for cost, time and delivery. The single arm is dropped (it does not use the hand-off layer and was measured in sweep-2).
declared_changes.why: A symmetric file-side fault (mutating the workers' out/ files) would corrupt the scored deliverables, race with the workers' own writes inside a live sandbox and change what is scored; it is not defensible. So every decision measure (catch rate, false rejects, republish cycles) is treatment-only: a mechanism measurement, not a comparison.
declared_changes.earlier_result: the sweep-2 baseline rerun (29 of 33, $18.17) stays on record

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: Carried over from parallel-sweep-2: every USD figure is in harness dollars (1.5x the Sonnet 5.5 list rates); the owner is to reconcile with the invoice. Recorded as cost_units_note in the fixture record.
declared_changes.why: An open question, recorded instead of assumed either way.

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: Carried over from parallel-sweep-2: every role of both arms runs with no node and no code-execution tool (policy.sandbox.denyExec, allowTools limited to Bash, Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, Glob and Grep, Bash network limited to localhost); verification by the synthesiser is therefore by reading code.
declared_changes.why: Running the corpus code would be one call for every value.

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: Carried over from parallel-sweep-2: every role of both arms runs with its real $HOME write-protected (policy.sandbox.homeWriteAllow: only ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.gemini are real, writable paths), and the kit's real-state check voids a trial on a stray entry in the home.
declared_changes.why: A role in the first parallel-sweep trio created ~/f7.sh in the real home.

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (lead decision; design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: The hand-off metrics reported a document's natural_errors only for versions the injector had not changed, so a producer's own error in a faulted document was invisible. HandoffStore now keeps what the producer sent for each version the injector changed (state.originals, by doc#version; doc_read never returns it), and handoff-metrics.mjs computes natural_errors from that original. Nothing a role sees, no fault class, no seed and no scoring changes.
declared_changes.why: In the p1t trial worker-1's on-disk sheets and its own doc_publish input listed every chain leaf-first instead of entry-first (a natural producer error, 0 of 12 per module); its document was a faulted one, so the harness reported no natural errors for w1. The injector never touches the producer's files, so the faulted document was wrong with or without the files-order fault.
declared_changes.earlier_result: the p1t result stays on record as measured (25 of 33 units, 1 of 4 faults caught) with this caveat: the files-order fault in w1 was confounded with the producer's own ordering error, so that fault's 'missed' outcome is not a clean measure

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (lead decision; design the next fixture variant where the synthesiser reads and decides on the published module documents; pick its pilot and run it if within plan, under about $150)
declared_changes.what: The synthesiser's caps are resized in both arms: budget_usd $3.0 to $5.0 (CAPS.synthesiser 1.5 to 2.5 in Haiku-price units, scaled by 2 on the production profile) and an explicit budget_tokens of 12,000,000 (SYNTHESISER_TOKENS in the kit). The org stop and planning allocation stay $34: the role caps now sum to 8 x 3.4 + 1.4 + 5.0 = $33.6, under it. Deadline, faults, roster, workers' and lead's USD caps are unchanged. With its own budget_tokens the runtime splits the rest of the org's 60 M over the other nine roles, 5.33 M each.
declared_changes.why: In p1t the synthesiser had no budget_tokens of its own, so it got the even split of the org's 60 M over 10 roles (6 M) and was closed at 444 s with 6.16 M used ($2.84, 81 % of its $3 cap, mostly cache reads, about 16.6 K tokens/s and $0.0063/s while active), before it had decided the last document or written the final synthesis. The whole 720 s deadline at that rate is about 11.8 M tokens and $4.5, so 12 M and $5.0 keep the cap from binding before the clock. Other roles at stage 1: workers 1.8 to 3.6 M tokens and $1.4 to $2.4, lead 1.4 M and $0.82; the org used 25.5 M of its 60 M. The baseline arm shares the numbers; its synthesiser aggregates files and uses far less.
declared_changes.earlier_result: the p1t result stays on record as measured (the synthesiser's token budget closed it at 444 s and the take-over was refused by policy), with the caveat that the cap, not the decision loop, ended its work

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction (lead decision; spec open items 17 and 18: the runtime relays a rejected document to its producer, and a deliverable-consistency check plus a verification aid for the consumer); the sweep-3 v1 results stay on record
declared_changes.what: A declared variant v2 of the parallel-sweep-3 treatment arm (pilot manifest variants[0], trial ids p<n>t-v2), built unpaid and test-first in the harness only (no change in src/orgrt): (17) when the consumer rejects a document the store has the harness deliver a message to the producing role (document, version, contract, reason, attempts left, what to do) and a short copy to the lead, through the daemon's own deliver, so the cross-section send refusal still applies; (18a) each document's contract declares its deliverable files (out/<module>/answers.json per sheet) and the fields that must match, a publish that disagrees is refused naming the file and the first differing field (5 such refusals per document, apart from the 4 publish attempts) and an accept is refused if a file changed since the publish; the comparison uses what the producer sent, never the copy the injector changed; (18b) a new consumer tool pilot__doc_check runs the contract's declared checks (value_type, files_match_evidence, value_matches_chain, files_in_module, unique_across_sheets; an unknown check type makes the contract invalid) over the document alone, and each answer in the published documents carries a document-only evidence list. The treatment arm (v1) is unchanged: same code paths, contracts, task text and tests.
declared_changes.why: The sweep-3 results: pooled over two treatment trials the synthesiser caught 3 of 8 injected faults (duplicate-sheet 2 of 2, files-order 1 of 2, wrong-value 0 of 4); the store does not tell a producer of a rejection, so the rejection went synthesiser to lead to worker (it worked, but depended on a lead relaying); worker-1 in p2t wrote bare arrays to out/m1..m4 while its published document was correct and accepted, so acceptance did not certify the scored file; and workers put the injected faults down to their own transcription errors. The change tests whether a direct relay, a consistency check between document and files, and a deterministic aid close those gaps.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none rewritten: the sweep-3 treatment results (p1t, p2t), the baseline control p1b and the committed v1 design, contracts and task text stay as measured; v2 trials carry the id suffix -v2 and are never paired with them. Not measured on a model yet.

variants.description: The treatment arm with the producer relay, deliverable consistency, doc_check and evidence in the documents (fixture.variants.v2); the same faults (seed_base plus the trial number, so p1t-v2 and p2t-v2 get the p1t and p2t placements), roster, caps and deadline; the baseline control stays as is.

stage_1.gates: the synthesiser made at least one successful pilot__doc_read call and at least one successful pilot__doc_check call in the trial; with 0 of either the mechanism failed: stop and report

stage_2.gate: only after the stage 1 v2 trial passed both gates
